name: Public safety
tagline: Fire, policing, paramedics, and emergency management: who delivers each, at what depth, and at what cost.
primer: Public safety in a rural Ontario township is delivered by four services owned at three different levels of government, and confusing them is the most common error in municipal debate. Fire is the township's. Policing is delivered by the Ontario Provincial Police and paid for by the township under a provincial billing model, which means council controls the bill's inputs only indirectly. Land ambulance is the United Counties'. Emergency management is a statutory township duty with a provincial compliance requirement.

The township's fire service is almost certainly a volunteer or composite service, and that fact shapes every number in this domain. A volunteer service does not have crews sitting in a station waiting; firefighters respond from home or work to the station and then to the call. Response time therefore has a component — turnout — that a career service does not have, and comparing a volunteer service's response time to a career service's benchmark measures the staffing model rather than the service's performance.

Ontario Regulation 378/18 requires every municipality to complete a community risk assessment and to use it in determining the services it provides. That document, and the fire master plan built from it, is where council's chosen depth of response is written down. It is the only fair benchmark for the service, because it is the standard council itself set. Where a response time is shown in this domain, what is measured — from dispatch, from notification, from turnout — is stated beside it, since the same service can produce very different numbers under different definitions.

Volunteer recruitment and retention is the leading indicator for the entire fire service. Apparatus can be bought and stations can be built; a roster cannot be purchased. Roster size, and the number of firefighters actually available for a weekday daytime call, are different figures, and the second is the one that determines what happens on a Tuesday morning.

Policing cost is the largest single public safety line in most rural township budgets and the one over which council has the least direct control. Under the provincial billing model, a municipality's bill is driven by a base cost per property and a calls-for-service component, both calculated provincially. Council can influence the second slowly and cannot change the first. Detachment statistics cover the detachment's service area, which typically spans several municipalities and does not match the township boundary.

Apparatus replacement is the one place in this domain where the township has full control and a long horizon. Fire apparatus has a defined service life, replacement is expensive, and the funded status of the replacement schedule connects directly to the reserve balances in the financial domain.

tierSplit.note: Township owns the service, the stations, and the apparatus, and sets the level of service.
Through the Stormont, Dundas and Glengarry OPP Detachment Board, a body appointed under provincial process rather than a township committee.
Delivered by the OPP, paid for by the township under the provincial billing model. Confirm whether the township has a police services board and its composition.
SDG delivers paramedic services county-wide and sets the council-approved response time standard.
Statutory township duty under the Emergency Management and Civil Protection Act, with annual compliance filed provincially.

Delivered through the fire service under the Fire Protection and Prevention Act.

gaps: Response time may not be recorded or reported at all. Where it is, confirm the measurement definition before comparing any two years — a change in dispatch software or reporting practice can move the figure without anything changing on the ground.
Daytime availability of volunteer firefighters is rarely reported even where roster size is. It is the more decision-relevant figure and may have to be requested from the fire chief directly.
Detachment-level policing statistics cover a service area larger than the township. Township-level crime statistics may not exist in publishable form.
Paramedic response time is reported county-wide by SDG. A township-level split may be obtainable but is not routinely published.

The township publishes only that the fire service has 'over fifty' volunteers across three stations. An exact year-end roster, and the split by station, must come from the fire chief or an annual report to council.

indicators.name: Fire service incidents, all types
indicators.geography: Township of North Glengarry — three stations: Alexandria, Apple Hill, Maxville
indicators.definition: Total incidents responded to during the year across all incident types, including medical assist, motor vehicle collision, alarm, and fire. Structure fires are a small minority of any modern fire service's call volume; the composition is in the detail table.

indicators.name: Volunteer firefighter roster
indicators.geography: Township of North Glengarry fire service
indicators.definition: Number of volunteer firefighters on the roster at year end across all three stations — Alexandria, Apple Hill and Maxville. The township describes the service as a contingent of over fifty volunteers, which is the only published figure and is not precise enough to anchor a series. Roster size is not the same as the number available to respond to a given call, particularly on weekdays.
indicators.methodology: Three stations covering 643 square kilometres, staffed by volunteers responding from home or work. That geography and that staffing model together determine what any response figure can mean.

indicators.name: Fire response time, 90th percentile
indicators.geography: Township of North Glengarry fire service area
indicators.tierNote: Township service. Response performance reflects a volunteer or composite staffing model chosen by council.
indicators.definition: Elapsed time from dispatch notification to arrival of the first apparatus on scene, at the 90th percentile. Measured from dispatch, which excludes call-taking time and includes turnout. This definition must accompany the figure: a service measuring from a different start point will produce a different number for identical performance.
indicators.methodology: Ninetieth percentile rather than average, because the average conceals the long tail and it is the tail that determines outcome. Comparison against any national standard designed for career services would measure the staffing model rather than the service; the applicable benchmark is the depth of response council adopted in the fire master plan.

indicators.name: Policing cost to the township
indicators.tierNote: Service delivered by the OPP under the provincial billing model; cost borne by the township levy.
indicators.definition: Annual amount billed to the township for policing services, as recorded in the budget and audited statements. Comprises a base cost driven by property count and a calls-for-service component, both calculated provincially. Governance runs through the Stormont, Dundas and Glengarry OPP Detachment Board. County-wide OPP costs rose sharply for 2025 — reported as up 13.19 percent on the budgeted 2024 amount and about 20.40 percent once a year-end adjustment was applied — but those are SDG-wide figures and the township's own billing statement is the only correct source for this line.

indicators.name: Policing cost per property
indicators.definition: Annual policing cost divided by the number of properties used in the provincial billing calculation. Shown because the total moves with property count as well as with cost, and the two causes are not distinguishable from the total alone.

indicators.name: Fire apparatus past recommended service life
indicators.geography: Township of North Glengarry fire service
indicators.definition: Count of front-line fire apparatus operating beyond the service life stated in the apparatus replacement schedule. Apparatus age can affect insurance grading for the properties the service protects, which is a consequence outside the township's budget.

tables.title: Fire service incidents by type
tables.description: Composition of call volume. Growth in medical assist and motor vehicle calls rather than in fires is the pattern in most Ontario services, and it changes what training, equipment, and staffing the service actually needs.
tables.geography: Township of North Glengarry fire service area

tables.title: Apparatus and major equipment: age, replacement, funded status
tables.description: Funded status answers whether a reserve balance exists to cover the replacement when it falls due. An unfunded replacement is a future levy increase, a future debenture, or a deferral.
tables.geography: Township of North Glengarry fire service
tables.note: Station names are correct: the service operates from Alexandria, Apple Hill and Maxville. Unit numbering, years, costs and funded status are placeholders until the apparatus replacement schedule is obtained. Whether an aerial apparatus is required at all is a level-of-service decision set in the fire master plan and the community risk assessment, not an automatic replacement.

tables.title: Emergency management programme currency
tables.description: The Emergency Management and Civil Protection Act sets annual requirements. Currency is checkable and binary: each item is either current or it is not.

Hazard identification and risk assessment review

tables.title: Paramedic services, county-delivered
tables.description: Land ambulance is an upper-tier service. Cornwall SDG Paramedic Services provides 24-hour, 365-day coverage to over 111,000 residents across the counties and the City of Cornwall. These figures describe that whole service area, not North Glengarry, because that is the geography at which they are reported. They are shown so the service is visible to a township reader, and labelled so they are not mistaken for township figures.
tables.geography: United Counties of Stormont, Dundas and Glengarry
tables.note: A township-level split of these figures may be obtainable from the county on request but is not routinely published. Do not attribute a county-wide figure to North Glengarry.
